text:
talia: Heads-up: legal hold was set for customer 0xC456 this morning but our nightly purge ran and found ~12 embeddings queued. We need an immediate stop and clarity on whether RBAC or KMS interactions could have let the purge bypass holds. Anyone able to look?

sandy (SRE): Pulling logs now. If purge saw a missing hold flag it should have skipped. cc @eva

eva (Security): I see the purge run, timestamps line up. Purger attempted to read metadata from keystore-wrapper and got a KMS error, then proceeded to delete local items anyway (looks like error handling swallowed the fail). Log snippet:
```
2026-03-19T03:08:12Z purger INFO fetch-meta subject=0xC456
2026-03-19T03:08:12Z purger ERROR kms:GetSecretValue AccessDenied for principal service-account:purger
2026-03-19T03:08:12Z purger WARN meta missing, defaulting to allow-delete
2026-03-19T03:08:13Z purger INFO delete embedded_id=emb_9d2
```

michael (Legal): Legal hold was set at 2026-03-18T23:22:01Z by legal:team. This is critical — do NOT allow any deletions until we verify scope and produce a forensic snapshot. We cannot have an "admin override" that quietly deletes items.

talia: Understood. Short-term mitigation: pause the scheduled purge job and run a dry-run to enumerate changes. Longer-term we should change the purge to be fail-safe: if metadata fetch from KMS fails, abort the entire job rather than defaulting to allow-delete. Also propose we store an immutable audit event in the audit-index for any legal hold so purger checks that index as an authoritative source.

carmen (Platform): Two KMS notes: 1) If a key was rotated and old versions removed we could lose the ability to decrypt metadata — that must not be allowed for records under legal hold. 2) We need to ensure KMS IAM bindings prevent the purge service principal from performing key deletion/rotation actions. KMS logs (key_id, operation, principal) must be forwarded to SIEM.

sandy (SRE): Immediate actions I started: paused scheduled purge, created ticket INF-3421, and kicked an adhoc snapshot of related S3 prefixes. Running manual dry-run next.
ops-bot: incident created: INF-3421 assigned to talia, priority P2. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3421

talia: Proposed RBAC change: create a role "legal:hold-manager" that can set/unset legal holds; only principals in the "legal:attorney" and "security:investigator" groups can lift holds. No single admin should be able to lift without 2-person approval (breakglass) and an automated audit entry that includes reason + ticket link.

eva (Security): +1 on the two-person breakglass. Also: purge service credentials should only have KMS decrypt/encrypt for a narrow key and never key management rights. Add an additional check in purge pipeline to query the audit-index for a LegalHold event before any delete. If KMS fetch fails, bail and alert oncall.

michael (Legal): We also need the DSAR runbook updated: on a deletion request we must first query keystore flags and audit-index, request a forensic snapshot, and escalate to security if anything is inconsistent. Legal needs a clear "can-we-delete" signoff flow. Update timeframe: escalate to security within 2 hours of detection.

talia: Implementation plan (ETA 48h):
- Pause purger scheduled triggers (done)
- Add pre-check: audit-index query for active holds
- Change error handling: KMS read failure => ABORT purge run + alert
- Create RBAC role legal:hold-manager and enforce 2-person lift
- Harden KMS IAM (no delete/rotate by purge principal) + SIEM ingestion of KMS logs
- Run forensic snapshot and handoff to legal

sandy (SRE): Running the pause now:```bash
/scripts/purger/ctl pause --reason \"legal hold 0xC456\"
```

ops-bot: Pause acknowledged for purger (user=sandy). INF-3421 status=investigating.

talia: I'll draft a short policy blurb for DSAR/retention exceptions so product+support know to raise holds via legal. Will send PR to docs and an RFC for RBAC/KMS in eng-security. Anyone want to be on the design review?

eva (Security): I'll join the review and help craft the detection + alerting requirements.

michael (Legal): I'll provide the hold lifecycle wording and confirmation checklist.

Note: do NOT implement any deletion-overrides in the name of "expediency". If a vulnerability leads to potential exfil we should automatically set holds and follow IR playbook, not bypass them.
